issue_title: [Bug]: STM32H5 missing } build failure with c++
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]: STM32H5 missing } build failure with c++

Body:
### Bug Summary

 When building with cpp, the H5 HAL errors out due to a missing }.

### Detailed Description

Originally discovered [on zephyr](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/105698)
When building with cpp, the H5 HAL errors out due to a missing }. 

This seems to be an issue with the HAL header stack. In stm32h5xx_hal_mdf.h, #ifdef __cplusplus
 block is placed before the MDF1 conditional is closed. This breaks compilation.
Moving it after the MDF1 close seems to fix the issue.


### Expected Behavior

Build Succeeds

### Actual Behavior

Build crashes with missing } error

### Environment

Build with cpp enabled on zephyr

### Severity

Major

issue_title: Misleading bitoperation in OEMiROT_Boot clock configuration
clean_text:
Title: Misleading bitoperation in OEMiROT_Boot clock configuration

Body:
**Describe the bug**
In the OEMiROT_Boot application (Projects/*/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot) there is this block in SetSysClock:


MODIFY_REG(RCC->PLL1CFGR, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1RGE, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1SRC_1 << RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1RGE_Pos);
MODIFY_REG(RCC->PLL1CFGR, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1VCOSEL, RCC_PLL1VCOWIDE << RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1VCOSEL_Pos);


PLL1RGE and PLL1SRC are unrelated fields in the register. Also RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1SRC_1 is already shifted to the right position in stm32h503xx.h

#define RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1SRC_1              (0x2UL << RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1SRC_Pos)     /*!< 0x00000002 */

The line generates the correct bit pattern, but purely by chance.

The shift in the 2nd line is also incorrect. Since RCC_PLL1VCOWIDE = 0, it does not do anything. But if you would use RCC_PLL1VCOMEDIUM instead, it would expand to this:

(0x1UL << RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1VCOSEL_Pos) << RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1VCOSEL_Pos

Yet again, the line generates the correct bit pattern, but purely by chance.

**Suggested Fix**
It should be replaced with a clearer alternative:


MODIFY_REG(RCC->PLL1CFGR, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1RGE, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1RGE_1);
MODIFY_REG(RCC->PLL1CFGR, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1VCOSEL, RCC_PLL1VCOWIDE);


or


MODIFY_REG(RCC->PLL1CFGR, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1RGE, RCC_PLL1_VCIRANGE_2);
MODIFY_REG(RCC->PLL1CFGR, RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1VCOSEL, RCC_PLL1VCOWIDE);

issue_title: image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.c is compiled and linked into the application on 2nd build in STM32CubeIDE
clean_text:
Title: image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.c is compiled and linked into the application on 2nd build in STM32CubeIDE

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
*  STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0

**Problem statement**
Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE
The project config has a build step that preprocesses OEMiROT_Boot/Src/image_macros_to_preprocess_bl2.c to OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.c which will serve as input data to postbuild.sh

If you build the project again, Eclipse CDT will pick up the new source file and compile it and provide it as an object when linking OEMiROT_Boot.elf.

The STM32CubeIDE/Debug/image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.o has empty .text, .data and .bss sections, so the only effect on the elf is some extra debug info which will be stripped away when creating the .bin-file to flash onto the MCU.

It does cause the linking step to be repeated on each build since the build step that preprocesses will change the timestamp of OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.c causing a re-build and re-link. On any reasonable developer box, this takes 10 seconds or less so it is not a biggie. And re-linking will happen anyway since the timestamp of output.ld changes.

**Suggested improvement**
Still - it would be beneficial if the image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.c was generated into the Release or Debug build-directory to keep CDT from picking it up.

postbuild.sh could be modified to get the path to the build directory and pick up image_macros_preprocessed_bl2.c from there and also put the logfile in the same directory. This would cause less pollution of the source directory which is always beneficial - especially in CI context.

issue_title: Remove redundant pre-processor symbol MCUBOOT_TARGET_CONFIG
clean_text:
Title: Remove redundant pre-processor symbol MCUBOOT_TARGET_CONFIG

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0

**Describe the bug**
Projects/*/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot

All the IDE-configs seem to add '-DMCUBOOT_TARGET_CONFIG=<flash_layout.h>' to the build command line.
I have only tested with STM32CubeIDE but it is present in EWARM/Project.ewp and MDK-ARM/Project.uvprojx too.

This preprocessor symbol is redundant. No code tests for it.

In the upstream mcuboot 1.7.2 it is used in boot/zephyr/include/target.h but this file is not present in  Middlewares/Third_Party/mcuboot/ in this git. There is no Zephyr support in this git. And to my understanding (which I admit is limited), if you want to boot Zephyr using mcuboot, you build mcuboot as part of Zephyr. OEMiROT_Boot cannot be used for this purpose.

**Suggested fix**
Remove '-DMCUBOOT_TARGET_CONFIG=<flash_layout.h>' from the project configs for EWARM, MDK-ARM and STM32CubeIDE.

issue_title: Remove redundant Debug/Release parameter to postbuild.sh
clean_text:
Title: Remove redundant Debug/Release parameter to postbuild.sh

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 *  STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0

**Describe the bug**
The STM32CubeIDE/postbuild.sh files (17 in total for the different projects) have code like this:

# arg2 is the config type (Debug, Release)
config=$2

And are called from STM32CubeIDE with the currently selected build type as positional parameter. For
$Project/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/postbuild.sh, the parameter is $1 but the rest of the description applies.

The parameter is not used since [v1.5.0](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/releases/tag/v1.5.0) when the code in postbuild.sh to copy the bin-file from the build output directory to Binary was replaced by a STM32CubeIDE postbuild step calling arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary … to generate the binfile.

This can be a bit confusing for developers who may think "surely this must have some effect somewhere but I can't find out where".

**Suggested fix**
Remove the remaining handling of parameter config from postbuild.sh and STM32CubeIDE's adding of the build config positional parameter.

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
*  STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0

**Describe the bug**
Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/.cproject has

 <option IS_BUILT
IN_EMPTY="false" IS_VALUE_EMPTY="false" id="com.st.stm32cube.ide.mcu.gnu.managed
build.tool.c.compiler.option.definedsymbols.1729823404" name="Define symbols (-D
)" superClass="com.st.stm32cube.ide.mcu.gnu.managedbuild.tool.c.compiler.option.
definedsymbols" useByScannerDiscovery="false" valueType="definedSymbols">
    <listOptionValue builtIn="false" value="OEMUROT_ENABLE_NO"/>

for both debug and release builds. This can also be seen in the UI in
File / Properties / C/C++ Build / Settings / MCU GCC Compiler / Preprocessor / Define symbols where OEMUROT_ENABLE_NO is shown in the list.

This will add -DOEMUROT_ENABLE_NO to the command line when building the project.

This preprocessor symbol is redundant. No code tests for it. The code tests for OEMUROT_ENABLE.
To my understanding from https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/wiki/Security:OEMiRoT_OEMuRoT_for_STM32H5, OEMUROT_ENABLE should not be set for STM32H563 as it does not support OEMuROT since it requires STiROT which is only available on STM32H33 and STM32H573.

**Suggested fix**
Remove pre-processor symbol OEMUROT_ENABLE_NO from STM32CubeIDE's build config.

I don't think it is defined for the other MCUs in Project/ or for the the EWARM and MDK-ARM toolchains. But I don't have those tools so I can just grep in the project configs. Please remove it from those also if it is actually present.

issue_title: Trustzone project problem - STM32H563ZIT
clean_text:
Title: Trustzone project problem - STM32H563ZIT

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * Nucleo-H563ZI
 * AC6 6.23 & 6.24

***Describe the bug***

I have created a Trustzone program with the STM32H563ZIT (nucleo board) as an example for a course. I use uVision for the course because of the debugging possibilities.  Compiler was AC6 6.23.

To be able to demonstrate the TZ-processes well, I have set the compiler optimization for both projects to O0.

**Secure & Non-Secure O0**

The following problem has occurred:

* The program starts normally Secure.
* The change to Non-Secure works.
* When calling the __HAL_PWR_VOLTAGESCALING_CONFIG() macro in the SystemClock_Config()  function and the following waiting loop called by main(), an exception occurs (NMI Secure). 

The problem does not only occur during debugging. Even a reset button or poweron does not cause the program to work.


**Secure O0 & Non-Secure O1**

Since the program worked before, I set the compiler optimization of NS-Project to -O1. After that, the problem no longer occurred. The program also runs on reset or poweron.


**Secure & Non-Secure O0   & Stopover**

As I wanted to find the cause of the problem, I set the NS project back to -O0. The problem occurred again. When debugging, the exception could be avoided by setting a breakpoint to the line after the macro call. The program also worked with this breakpoint. With reset or poweron the program could not be started correctly.


**Secure & Non-Secure O0   & __ISB()**

My assumption is that certain machine instructions must be completed before the next line can be accessed. To ensure this, I inserted the __ISB(); instruction. After that the program worked with the compiler settings O0 and O1. This also applies to Reset.


**Keil Studio Compiler 6.24 & __ISB()**
  
I have also set up the same project in KeilStudio (windows) (compiler 6.24). There the problem could not be solved by changing the compiler optimization. Here the program only worked without an intermediate stop by inserting __ISB().


**Conclusion**

Since the customization in the SystemClock_Config() function is overwritten with CunbeMX each time code is generated, the workaround is unsatisfactory.

All programs with deactivated Trustzone work without the need for a change.


***Changed Code***


void SystemClock_Config(void)
{
  RCC_OscInitTypeDef RCC_OscInitStruct = {0};
  RCC_ClkInitTypeDef RCC_ClkInitStruct = {0};

  /** Configure the main internal regulator output voltage
  */
  __HAL_PWR_VOLTAGESCALING_CONFIG(PWR_REGULATOR_VOLTAGE_SCALE0);

  __ISB();   // FE
  while(!__HAL_PWR_GET_FLAG(PWR_FLAG_VOSRDY)) {}

issue_title: Incorrect doc-string for FLASH_EraseInitTypeDef in `stm32h55xx_hal_flash_ex.h` ?
clean_text:
Title: Incorrect doc-string for FLASH_EraseInitTypeDef in `stm32h55xx_hal_flash_ex.h` ?

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * NUCLEO-H563ZI 
 * STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0

**Describe the bug**
FLASH_EraseInitTypeDef is defined as follows:


typedef struct
{
  uint32_t TypeErase;   /*!< Mass erase or sector Erase.
                             This parameter can be a value of @ref FLASH_Type_Erase */

  uint32_t Banks;       /*!< Select banks to erase when Mass erase is enabled.
                             This parameter can be a value of @ref FLASH_Banks
                             (FLASH_BANK_BOTH should be used only for mass erase) */

  uint32_t Sector;      /*!< Initial FLASH sector to erase when Mass erase is disabled
                             This parameter can be a value of @ref FLASH_Sectors */

  uint32_t NbSectors;   /*!< Number of sectors to be erased.
                             This parameter can be a value between 1 and (max number of sectors in the bank -
                             value of initial sector)*/
} FLASH_EraseInitTypeDef;




The Banks field is documented as Select banks to erase when Mass erase is enabled, but in the function HAL_FLASHEx_Erase that consumes the FLASH_EraseInitTypeDef struct, the Banks field is also accessed in the  case that the erase type is set to sectors (i.e. that the TypeErase field is set to FLASH_TYPEERASE_SECTORS) and not only when the erase type is mass erase. Is this intentional or a hiccup in the documentation?

Title: Redundant files OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/Example/Startup/startup_stm32h5*.s

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0

**Additional context**
The files Projects/NUCLEO-H533RE/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/Example/Startup/startup_stm32h533retx.s and Projects/NUCLEO-H563ZI/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/Example/Startup/startup_stm32h563zitx.s (they do not seem to exist for the other boards covered by this git) are redundant.

They contain a reset handler and interrupt vectors but these are never actually linked. The linker script in OEMiROT_Boot/STM32CubeIDE/stm32h5xx_bl2.ld links the implementations from OEMiROT_Boot/Src/startup_stm32h5xx.c which in turn partly relies on _mainCRTStartup from lib/gcc/arm-none-eabi/13.3.1/thumb/v8-m.main+fp/hard/crt*.o of the tool chain.

I assume these are left-overs from creating a new STM32CubeIDE project and then setting up the project to use the common OEMiROT and mcuboot code.

They confuse the customers trying to debug the Reset_Handler.

I suggest that they be removed from the project's sources.

issue_title: FIXME should be fixed or removed in #define OEMIROT_OB_BOOT_LOCK OB_BOOT_LOCK_ENABLE
clean_text:
Title: FIXME should be fixed or removed in #define OEMIROT_OB_BOOT_LOCK OB_BOOT_LOCK_ENABLE

Body:
In Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/Inc/boot_hal_cfg.h for projects NUCLEO-H533RE, NUCLEO-H563ZI and STM32H573I-DK
C
#ifdef OEMIROT_DEV_MODE
#define OEMIROT_OB_BOOT_LOCK OB_BOOT_LOCK_ENABLE /*!< BOOT Lock expected value  */
#define OEMIROT_ERROR_HANDLER_STOP_EXEC /*!< Error handler stops execution (else it resets) */
#else
#define OEMIROT_OB_BOOT_LOCK OB_BOOT_LOCK_ENABLE /*!< FIXME BOOT Lock expected value  */
#endif /* OEMIROT_DEV_MODE */


The FIXME doesn't seem relevant. OB_BOOT_LOCK_ENABLE (defined in stm32h5xx_hal_flash_ex.h) is 0xB4U which according to RM0481 means enabled so you won't be able to change SECBOOT_ADD or SWAP_BANK which makes the boot setup more secure.

But since this is security related SW, any FIXME comment causes some unease in code security review.

**Request**
Please either fix what needs to be fixed or remove the FIXME.

Title: warning: 'node_info.currentnode_addr' may be used uninitialized when using DMA with -Ofast compile flag

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
Custom board with STM32H523ZWTx
IDE: STM32CubeIDE 1.18.0
STM32Cube MCU Package and version: STM32H5 1.5.0

**Describe the bug**
When I try to use DMA with -Ofast or -O3 flag i got the following warning during compilation


../Drivers/STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_dma_ex.c: In function 'HAL_DMAEx_List_ConvertQToDynamic':
../Drivers/STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_dma_ex.c:2992:77: warning: 'node_info.currentnode_addr' may be used uninitialized [-Wmaybe-uninitialized]
 2992 |     if (((uint32_t)pQList->FirstCircularNode != 0U)                         &&
      |         ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~
 2993 |         ((uint32_t)pQList->FirstCircularNode != node_info.currentnode_addr) &&
      |         ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~  
../Drivers/STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_dma_ex.c:2939:26: note: 'node_info.currentnode_addr' was declared here
 2939 |   DMA_NodeInQInfoTypeDef node_info;
      |                          ^~~~~~~~~


**How To Reproduce**
1. Create a blank C code ST project for STM32H523ZET6 with library copy.
2. Enable USART1 as Asynchronous with Data Direction: Receive Only - other parameters default.
3. Enable GPDMA1 Channel 0 - 2 Words internal FIFO as Standard Request Mode
4. Configure the GPDMA1 Channel 0 as Circular Mode: Enable, Request: USART1_RX, Destination Address Increment After Transfer: Enabled - other parameters default.
5. In NVIC enable USART1 global interrupt.
6. Save and generate code - when prompted for enabling cache - ignore and click Yes.
7. Right click on your project and open the projects Properties. Go to C/C++ Build, Settings, Tool Settings, MCU/MPU GCC Compiler, Optimization and use Optimization level: Optimize for speed (-Ofast). Click Apply and Apply and Close.
8. Right click your project and click on Clean Project.
9. Click on the build icon.

**Attachments**
I added the exported project to this issue [dma-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19472574/dma-test.zip)

Hoping that there might be better luck here in the H5 repo :)

Short version:
It would be really beneficial to have a void* pointer in the HAL handles to associate any context that a user might need, which can be accessed in e.g. callbacks. This could make writing modular code and e.g. middleware simpler.

For details and discussions, see the attached issue in the G4 repo.

This feature could can potentially be enabled and disabled in config in the same way as registrable callbacks to prevent bloat.

Hoping this is something you could look into. Cheers!

In the GTZC Example:

With the latter after the call to NonSecure_ResetHandler() in NonSecure_Init(), the debugger goes straight to the HardFault_Handler() in the file XX_Secure/Core/Src/stm32h5xx-it.c

**How To Reproduce**
For both i followed the instructions of the [GTZC Illegal Access Readme](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/tree/main/Projects/STM32H573I-DK/Examples/GTZC/GTZC_MPCWM_IllegalAccess_TrustZone/README.md):
Open STM32CubeIDE
File > Import. Point to the STM32CubeIDE folder of the example project. Click Finish.
Select and build the xxxxx_NS project, this will automatically trigger build of xxxxx_S project
Select the xxxxx_S project and select “Debug configuration”
Double click on “STM32 Cortex-M C/C++ Application”
Select “Startup” > “Add” >
Select the xxxxx_NS project
Build configuration : Select Release/Debug
Click Debug to debug the example



I'd appreciate any help :)

[funkii7 - 2023-10-24T14:07:00Z]
I additionally examined the SCB registers which could be relevant when the execution lands in the hardfault handler: HFSR, CFSR, and BFAR.

The register values of the GTZC Illegal Access example are attached.

![hfsr](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/assets/47930933/da0985a9-a50a-4573-a887-fc42fd7906f3)
![bfar_cfsr](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/assets/47930933/d2c5b373-b90e-45fe-b768-f757a1a6f8b2)

[funkii7 - 2023-11-02T10:54:01Z]
Turns out i just forgot to set the Option Bytes as described in [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/tree/main/Projects/STM32H573I-DK/Examples/GTZC/GTZC_MPCWM_IllegalAccess_TrustZone):


User Option Bytes configuration:

Please note the internal Flash is fully secure by default in TZEN=0xB4 and User Option Bytes SECWM1_PSTRT/SECWM1_PEND and SECWM2_PSTRT/SECWM2_PEND should be set according to the application configuration. Here the proper User Option Bytes setup in line with the project linker/scatter file is as follows: - TZEN=0xB4 - SECWM1_PSTRT=0x0 SECWM1_PEND=0x7F meaning all 128 pages of Bank1 set as secure - SECWM2_PSTRT=0x1 SECWM2_PEND=0x0 meaning no page of Bank2 set as secure, hence Bank2 non-secure

issue_title: Bug in UCPD_InitStruct() function
clean_text:
Title: Bug in UCPD_InitStruct() function

Body:
[UCPD_InitStruct()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/blob/3d723b2467cdb13c2d780ceaa583b269680b67a4/Drivers/STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h5xx_ll_ucpd.c#L131) function is missing value lshift
is:
UCPD_InitStruct->psc_ucpdclk
should be:
(UCPD_InitStruct->psc_ucpdclk << UCPD_CFG1_PSC_UCPDCLK_Pos)
since UCPD_CFG1_PSC_UCPDCLK_Pos != 0

Btw, **PSC_UCPDCLK** name is inconsistent with registry description ([RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) section 74.8.1) - see https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_u5/issues/1

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2023-11-29T16:11:31Z]
Hi @tdjastrzebski,

Thank you for this report. From what I see, there is no need to shift the value of  UCPD_InitStruct->psc_ucpdclk before the assignment.

Indeed, the possible [values](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/blob/3d723b2467cdb13c2d780ceaa583b269680b67a4/Drivers/STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h5xx_ll_ucpd.h#L225-L232) taken by UCPD_InitStruct->psc_ucpdclk are **already shifted**.

This is not the case for the other attributes like UCPD_InitStruct->transwin that are meant to take [values](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/blob/3d723b2467cdb13c2d780ceaa583b269680b67a4/Drivers/STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h5xx_ll_ucpd.h#L60-L63) "between Min_Data=0x1 and Max_Data=0x1F" that are **not shifted**, thus **requiring the shift** operations.

I hope this makes things clearer. Please allow me to close this issue in this case.

With regards,

Hello,
It seems that there is an issue in the PLL1M configuration in _Projects/STM32H573I-DK/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/Src/system_stm32h5xx.c_ file _SetSysClock()_ function. **RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1M_Pos** was used as the value.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/blob/3d723b2467cdb13c2d780ceaa583b269680b67a4/Projects/STM32H573I-DK/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/Src/system_stm32h5xx.c#L298

Also, I think the values for reaching 250MHz should be like this:
- PLLM: 4 (RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1M_Pos will expand to 8)
- PLLN: 31 (it's 60 in the current code)
- PLLP: 2
- PLLQ: 2
- PLLR: 2
- PLLFRACN: 2048

**Screenshot**
![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/assets/86543823/5cd8af91-2a29-4540-a311-31d945124c29)

Furthermore, it might be better to use:
_RCC_PLL1_VCORANGE_WIDE_ instead of _RCC_PLL1VCOWIDE_
_RCC_PLL1_VCIRANGE_2_ instead of _RCC_PLL1CFGR_PLL1SRC_1_
_RCC_SYSCLKSOURCE_PLLCLK_ instead of _(RCC_CFGR1_SW_1 | RCC_CFGR1_SW_0)_

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH5/blob/3d723b2467cdb13c2d780ceaa583b269680b67a4/Projects/STM32H573I-DK/Applications/ROT/OEMiROT_Boot/Src/system_stm32h5xx.c#L297

issue_title: OB_BOR_LEVEL_x: probable error in stm32h5xx_hal_flash_ex.h file
clean_text:
Title: OB_BOR_LEVEL_x: probable error in stm32h5xx_hal_flash_ex.h file

Body:
Hi,
I think that the macros OB_BOR_LEVEL_1, OB_BOR_LEVEL_2 and OB_BOR_LEVEL_3 are wrong. They are defined in the STM32H5xx_HAL_Driver _stm32h5xx_hal_flash_ex.h_ header file, starting from line 305.

According to page 328 of the [reference manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0481-stm32h563h573-and-stm32h562-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) of the STM32H5, their values should be the following:

#define OB_BOR_LEVEL_1        (FLASH_OPTSR_BOR_LEV_1 | FLASH_OPTSR_BOR_LEV_0)  /*!< Reset level 1 threshold */
#define OB_BOR_LEVEL_2        FLASH_OPTSR_BOR_LEV_0                            /*!< Reset level 2 threshold */
#define OB_BOR_LEVEL_3        FLASH_OPTSR_BOR_LEV_1                            /*!< Reset level 3 threshold */

Thank you
Alessandro
